decisions.reason: The firm is expanding, has slack, and holds R&D and university/EU project capacity, so it can carry this fouling-detection automation while results are still uncertain, especially since it fits the firm's push toward digital monitoring of energy-recovery infrastructure.

A web tool for weir dimensioning is cheap to maintain and draws engineering planners toward the firm's core flood-control hardware, so no performance shortfall is likely to trigger search for other uses of the resources.

The fouling-detection system likely comes out of a funded research project and overlaps with Product A, so it may later be merged into it, but with turnover growing and the firm expanding, aspirations are being met and there is little pressure to drop it within a year.
